name: CalyxOS
summary: A privacy-oriented mobile operating system developed by The Calyx Institute based on the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), featuring built-in microG integration, Datura Firewall, Seedvault encrypted backups, and verified boot support across Pixel, Fairphone, and Motorola devices.
license: GPLv2 (Linux kernel) / Apache License 2.0 (AOSP userspace) & GPLv3/LGPL (various utilities)

content.introduction: CalyxOS is an open-source mobile operating system developed and maintained by The Calyx Institute, a non-profit organization dedicated to digital privacy and civil liberties. Based on the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), CalyxOS aims to deliver an accessible, privacy-respecting mobile experience by minimizing tracking, providing application-level firewall controls, and offering optional microG compatibility.
content.what_is_it: CalyxOS is a turnkey mobile distribution designed for everyday privacy without requiring deep technical expertise. It ships without proprietary Google Mobile Services, instead bundling open-source alternatives for application distribution, location resolution, encrypted cloud backups, and network protection, while enforcing verified boot with relocked bootloaders on supported hardware.
content.technical_base_android_platform_and_buil:
CalyxOS est construit sur l’Android Open Source Project, que le projet décrit comme la base des téléphones Android construits par des fabricants comme Samsung, et reprend largement du code et des pratiques de la communauté LineageOS. La couche applicative associe microG, réimplémentation libre des services Google Play, le client F-Droid Basic pour le catalogue FOSS et Aurora Store pour l’accès au catalogue de Google Play.

Les sources sont publiées sur `gitlab.com/CalyxOS` et recopiées sur `github.com/CalyxOS`, les contributions passant par une instance Gerrit de revue de code. La documentation de développement indique la branche `android17` : elle est synchronisée par `repo init --git-lfs -u https://gitlab.com/CalyxOS/platform_manifest -b android17`, suivi de `repo sync`. Les fichiers propriétaires d’un appareil s’obtiennent avec `./calyx/scripts/pixel/device.sh` et le nom de code de l’appareil, par exemple `akita` pour le Pixel 8a ; la construction s’effectue par `breakfast akita user` puis `m`, et l’installation par `fastboot flashall`. Le projet précise qu’une construction doit être signée pour permettre le verrouillage du chargeur d’amorçage, la variante `user` servant aux publications et la variante `userdebug` au développement.
content.microg_and_degoogling_approach: CalyxOS delivers a privacy-conscious mobile environment that strips out default Google telemetry, device trackers, and proprietary analytics services. To preserve broad application compatibility for mainstream users, CalyxOS integrates microG, the open-source re-implementation of Google Play Services. CalyxOS implements restricted signature spoofing, allowing only the cryptographically signed microG package to emulate Google Play Services identities while blocking arbitrary third-party applications from spoofing package signatures. Users have granular control to enable or disable microG features entirely, including Google Cloud Messaging (push notifications) and location providers (configured with privacy-preserving Mozilla Location Services or local Nominatim databases).
content.network_firewall_and_security_tools: A central component of CalyxOS is Datura Firewall, an integrated application-level firewall engineered by the Calyx Institute. Datura allows users to manage network permissions on a per-app basis, toggling access to Wi-Fi, cellular data, background connections, or blocking internet access entirely. Because Datura operates directly at the Android framework level using native Linux iptables/nftables rules, it does not occupy the device's single native Android VPN slot. This architecture allows users to run external third-party VPNs (such as CalyxVPN, WireGuard, or Mullvad) alongside active firewall policies. CalyxOS also enforces encrypted DNS by default, pre-configuring DNS-over-TLS servers (such as Cloudflare, Quad9, or custom resolvers) to prevent ISP DNS snooping.
content.backup_system_and_bundled_software: CalyxOS includes Seedvault, a comprehensive open-source backup solution built into the operating system settings. Developed under Calyx Institute sponsorship, Seedvault creates client-side encrypted backups of installed applications, application data, SMS messages, call logs, and system settings, storing them on external USB flash drives or remote Nextcloud instances via WebDAV. The default software bundle emphasizes verified open-source utilities: the Chromium-based Calyx Browser with built-in tracker protection, the F-Droid client with Privileged Extension for seamless background updates, the Signal encrypted messaging app, and Orbot for routing application traffic through the Tor anonymity network.
content.hardware_support_and_lifecycle: CalyxOS supports a curated list of smartphones that allow bootloader relocking with custom cryptographic signing keys, ensuring the integrity of Android Verified Boot (AVB). Supported hardware includes Google Pixel devices (Pixel 4a through Pixel 9 series), the modular Fairphone 4 and Fairphone 5, the SHIFT6mq, and select Motorola handsets (such as moto g32 and moto g52). The Calyx Institute delivers monthly security updates aligned with the Android Security Bulletin (ASB) via an encrypted over-the-air mechanism.
content.institutional_origin_and_release_chronol: CalyxOS is produced by the Calyx Institute, a non-profit organisation that describes its work as defending digital privacy and offers members a Pixel phone with CalyxOS preinstalled. Beyond the AOSP base, releases are split between security updates and feature updates, each published monthly. The release chronology recorded on the project news page runs as follows: CalyxOS 7.2.5.20 on Android 16 for all supported devices with the September 2026 security update; on 1 October 2026 the rollout of CalyxOS 8.0.0.0 on Android 17 began for part of the device list, followed on 5 October 2026 by an announcement of a device-specific release schedule. Releases had been interrupted earlier in 2026: the project published 7.2.2.0 on 1 July 2026 describing it as restored and as the build that would receive all future updates.
content.device_catalog_and_support_tiers: The project publishes three device tiers. Current devices include the Pixel 6 through Pixel 10a, Pixel Fold, Pixel Tablet, Fairphone 5, Fairphone (Gen. 6), SHIFTphone 8 and several Motorola models (moto g 5G 2024, g84 5G, g34 5G, g45 5G). Extended support covers the Pixel 4a (5G), Pixel 5, Pixel 5a (5G), Fairphone 4 and moto g52, g42 and g32. Older Pixel models and beta OnePlus builds are listed as no longer supported.
content.bundled_applications: CalyxOS ships a set of applications chosen for private communication: Signal for calls, messages and video, Tor Browser for web access, VPN services from Tor and Riseup, and the F-Droid and Aurora Store catalogues for applications. microG substitutes part of Google Play Services and is presented as optional. These applications are listed on the project's home page alongside the device list.
advantages: Privacy-by-default architecture eliminating Google tracking and invasive telemetry out of the box
Native Datura Firewall offering granular per-app control over Wi-Fi, cellular, and background data
Built-in Seedvault providing end-to-end encrypted backups to USB drives or Nextcloud/WebDAV servers
Integrated microG offering broad application compatibility with the option to disable it completely
Support for multiple hardware vendors (Pixel, Fairphone, Motorola) with verified boot enforcement
disadvantages: Hardware compatibility is restricted to devices supporting verified boot with custom relocking keys
MicroG does not provide complete compatibility with all proprietary Google Play Services APIs
Small non-profit development team compared to commercial smartphone operating system vendors
who_is_it_for: Everyday users seeking a straightforward, out-of-the-box de-Googled Android experience
Privacy advocates desiring granular application firewall control and encrypted remote backups
Owners of Fairphone, Pixel, or supported Motorola devices seeking a non-commercial open-source OS
who_is_it_not_for: Users requiring advanced kernel-level exploit mitigations and hardware memory tagging (MTE)
Users reliant on devices from manufacturers that prohibit bootloader relocking with custom keys
content.verdict: CalyxOS provides a balanced, user-friendly approach to mobile privacy on modern Android smartphones. By combining verified boot enforcement, a rootless per-app firewall, and optional microG integration, it bridges the gap between privacy protection and daily functional usability across multiple hardware brands.

components.note: Base platform: the project describes CalyxOS as an Android mobile operating system; the page does not name AOSP.

components.name: Datura Firewall
components.note: Firewall giving fine-grained control over network access for every application, listed among the system features.

components.name: Seedvault
components.note: Documented as Secure Backup with Seedvault: automatic backups once configured, optional backup to a USB drive or Nextcloud, and client-side encryption.

components.name: Verified Boot
components.note: Listed under device security: verified boot ensures that the operating system has not been modified.

relations.name: Android / AOSP

relations.note: Alternative community-driven Android distribution offering broader hardware support and CyanogenMod heritage.
